question: If invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") bills work or goods: how does it relate to what the purchase order, SOW or contract authorizes? Pick one.
options: Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") IS what the purchase order, SOW or contract authorizes: the priced item, milestone, period or deliverable itself, or the ordinary work an umbrella or retainer authorization describes. A line of a covered KIND of work counts even when its description is brief or generic (vagueness is a separate question). NOT this: a part of something another line already bills, an add-on or extra beyond the priced units (approved or not), or work the authorization never describes. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Where the PO states priced lines, those are the priced units and the scope text does not widen them. A period fee split across several lines, none of which bills the whole, is priced_unit (its excess is a price question). Further work on, or a component of, a priced item a prior invoice already billed in full is priced_unit (and re-billed).

Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") bills a PART of something ANOTHER line on this same invoice already bills in full, so the invoice charges that work twice: a flat monthly fee plus a prorated or catch-up charge for the same window, the same milestone under two labels, a component billed separately when another line's price already includes it by its own description, or hourly lines for work the retainer already covers (the retainer's scope as the contract or PO gives it, or as the line itself says it is included, not only the retainer line's printed words). NO for different roles, phases, sites, deliverables or periods of one project, for hourly lines for work OUTSIDE the retainer's scope, and for lines that merely share a generic description. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. The scope of a retainer, period-fee, milestone or fixed-price line is the scope the CONTRACT gives it, not the words of the invoice line: a line billed alongside such a line for the same window or milestone that describes work within that scope (or nothing more specific), or that itself says it is included under it, is YES; so is work the contract sum already obliges the contractor to perform (its own rework or punch-list items, an activity within a milestone) billed as a separate line. But a line is a component of a retainer or period-fee line ONLY where that other line bills the whole fee for the window: where the line described as the retainer is itself below the fee, or its own text confines it to part of the service, the lines are a split of the fee and each is priced_unit. Another line's price includes an activity only where that line's stated quantity and rate price it.

Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is work BEYOND the priced units (an hourly or daily add-on on a fixed-fee, retainer or milestone contract; a change; extra units) AND the packet shows it was approved in writing before or when it was done: a change order, a PO line for it, an email or approval comment from the designated approver naming it, or a verbal emergency approval that the contract itself permits. NO if the line is the priced work itself, or if no such written approval is in the packet. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. A change order is shown only where the change order itself, or a record of ours recording its approval, is in the packet; a record that merely mentions a change-order number does not show it. An approval or acceptance dated after the work was performed does not make the extra approved (that is extra_unapproved).

Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is work of a covered KIND beyond the priced units (an hourly or daily add-on on a fixed-fee, retainer or milestone contract; extra units; a change) WITHOUT written approval in the packet: a verbal request the contract does not provide for, a later tracker mention, an owner who says they asked informally, a pre-approval the packet never shows. NO if the line is the priced work itself, if written approval is in the packet, or if the work is of a kind the authorization never describes at all. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Also YES for in-scope work billed on a basis the contract does not provide (hourly or daily on a lump-sum, fixed-fee or milestone contract); for a line ordered without any purchase order under a framework agreement that authorizes work only through purchase orders; and for work the scope text admits only by change order when no change order is shown.

Invoice line 1 ("Managed Equipment Support Services retainer (prorated) — service period 28 Jun 2026 to 27 Jul 2026. Includes D1 preventive maintenance scheduling/coordination and dispatch tracking updates. Ref: PO-BHGF-2026-4962 / AG...") is NOT the work the authorization describes at all: a different service, deliverable or project, a kind of work the contract or PO scope text never mentions, or an item the PO or owner explicitly excludes. NO for an add-on of a covered kind that merely lacks its own approval, and for a line whose wording is too vague to place. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Work the contract's scope text expressly excludes is not_ours even if a change order could have added it. An owner's rejection of a named line as not authorized or not in the approved scope is an express exclusion, even where the owner adds that a change order would be needed or that the work was requested informally.
UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

question: Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. question: What IS invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.")? Pick the one kind that fits, from its own wording and the invoice.
options: Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") bills WORK OR GOODS: a service, deliverable, milestone, period of service, labour hours, usage, licences or physical items. Not tax, not a freight/handling/surcharge line, not a credit, discount, rebate, retainage or expense line.

Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") IS a tax amount (VAT, GST, IGST, sales tax, HST) charged on the other lines, whatever it is called. Work ABOUT tax (tax advisory, VAT return preparation, a tax compliance calendar) is work, not tax.

Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") is a CHARGE ON TOP of the work rather than work itself: freight, shipping, handling, courier, postage, a surcharge, an expediting, admin, processing or minimum charge, or a commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines. Freight booking or dispatch paperwork accompanying goods is a charge on top; a line that itself delivers a service or goods is work.

Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") is a CREDIT, discount, rebate or credit-memo line, whether shown negative or (wrongly) positive. It reduces or adjusts what is owed rather than billing work.

Invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") is an EXPENSE pass-through (travel, per diem, mileage reimbursement) or a retainage / retention release line. Billed usage of a service (fleet mileage as the service itself) is work, not an expense.

question: If invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") bills work or goods: what do OUR OWN records establish about whether it was performed or delivered for the billed period? Pick one. The vendor's own documents never move a line out of vendor_only.
options: OUR OWN records (a goods receipt, receiving confirmation, acceptance record, owner tracker note, owner comment or an unqualified owner approval) say the work or goods on invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") were delivered or performed as billed for the billed period or milestone, or delivered with only the formal sign-off still pending. A record that describes the deliverable as a whole confirms every line of it. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality. NO if our record says less or nothing was done, if only the vendor's own documents describe it, or if nothing describes it. A record describing the deliverable or service period as a whole confirms every line the packet places within it, including hourly or add-on lines for that period, unless it names the line's work as missing or incomplete; a record that itemises what it reviewed confirms only the items it names, and a record that names the period or deliverable and then lists what it comprised or what was checked IS an itemising record. Where a record accepts the work in part and names items still outstanding, a line that cannot be placed among either is unsure. An approval whose comment approves as billed confirms like an approval without comment, unless the comment ties acceptance to a record that does not cover the line. A delivered item with a minor, remediable defect is confirmed. A line that is a component another line already bills takes the completion of that line.

OUR OWN record says LESS was done or delivered on invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") than the line bills: a lower percent complete, fewer units or a smaller headcount, components not fitted, deliverables the owner says are missing, receiving short (an acceptance record, or a goods receipt when there is no acceptance record). Only the buyer's own words count. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality; a goods receipt plainly wrong for lines other records verify is disregarded. NO if our record says nothing was done at all, if the disagreement is about whether the work was AUTHORISED (scope) or about price, or if the only conflicting document is the vendor's. Also YES for a deliverable our record says was delivered but nonconforming or requiring revision before acceptance. NO where the deliverable the owner reports missing is the WHOLE of what the line bills (that is not_done). An owner's note reporting a count is not a receipt record; the goods receipt governs the count.

Our own records, or the vendor's own admission in the thread, say the work or goods on invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") have NOT HAPPENED AT ALL: not started, nothing delivered, milestone not reached. Partly done, done differently, fewer units or a lower percent complete is NO (that is 'less'). A milestone billed before its acceptance with no record saying the work has not happened is NO. A single deliverable that the owner's record says has not been received is not_done, not less.

The ONLY evidence describing the work or goods on invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") is the vendor's own: its service log, its report, its delivery note, its timesheet. Nothing from our side (receipt, receiving, acceptance, owner note or an approval without comment) describes this line's work as delivered, short or not done. NO only if such a record of ours exists (a note that our review is still pending is not one), or if nothing at all describes it. The vendor's own evidence includes a timesheet or transmittal reproduced on or attached to the invoice, and the vendor's assertion in an email or in the invoice's own narrative that the work was performed. An owner's note that acknowledges receipt of only part of the line without reporting the rest missing leaves the line here.

NOTHING in the packet describes the work or goods on invoice line 2 ("Initial registration questionnaire preparation — CFS Ltd.: Prepare entity registration questionnaires and supporting documentation checklist for state tax registrations.") as delivered or performed for the billed period: no record of ours and no vendor document either. Unqualified owner approval of the invoice counts as our record (then NO). A record describing a deliverable as a whole confirms only lines the packet places within that deliverable; a line the packet does not so place, described nowhere but by its own text and amount, is none.
UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

question: Take the price basis the contract or SOW text states for what this invoice bills, and compare like with like: ex-tax, net of any escalation or indexation the contract itself permits. If the basis is a TOTAL fee for the engagement: everything billed so far including this invoice (exact_facts.cumulative_billed is the structured figure; add paid priors if it is missing) exceeds it. If it is a fee PER PERIOD: this invoice's substantive lines together bill more than the fee for the period. If it is RATES or fixed milestone amounts: a line, or a milestone or period billed across several lines taken together, is billed higher than its stated rate or amount. If it is only a CAP: cumulative billing exceeds a cap that appears only in the prose; a cap that is also the PO's structured maximum or the contract's structured maximum is compared by code, and when the prose figure conflicts with the structured one the structured one governs, so NO. Billing at or below the basis is NO. If the text states no price for what is billed, NO. If the invoice currency differs from the currency of the stated basis, NO (no comparison is made).
options: The invoice, measured the way the stated basis requires, is above the stated figure.
At or below the figure, an escalation the contract permits, a tax-inclusive total compared with an ex-tax fee, or no figure stated.

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

question: If invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") bills work or goods: how does it relate to what the purchase order, SOW or contract authorizes? Pick one.
options: Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") IS what the purchase order, SOW or contract authorizes: the priced item, milestone, period or deliverable itself, or the ordinary work an umbrella or retainer authorization describes. A line of a covered KIND of work counts even when its description is brief or generic (vagueness is a separate question). NOT this: a part of something another line already bills, an add-on or extra beyond the priced units (approved or not), or work the authorization never describes. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Where the PO states priced lines, those are the priced units and the scope text does not widen them. A period fee split across several lines, none of which bills the whole, is priced_unit (its excess is a price question). Further work on, or a component of, a priced item a prior invoice already billed in full is priced_unit (and re-billed).

Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") bills a PART of something ANOTHER line on this same invoice already bills in full, so the invoice charges that work twice: a flat monthly fee plus a prorated or catch-up charge for the same window, the same milestone under two labels, a component billed separately when another line's price already includes it by its own description, or hourly lines for work the retainer already covers (the retainer's scope as the contract or PO gives it, or as the line itself says it is included, not only the retainer line's printed words). NO for different roles, phases, sites, deliverables or periods of one project, for hourly lines for work OUTSIDE the retainer's scope, and for lines that merely share a generic description. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. The scope of a retainer, period-fee, milestone or fixed-price line is the scope the CONTRACT gives it, not the words of the invoice line: a line billed alongside such a line for the same window or milestone that describes work within that scope (or nothing more specific), or that itself says it is included under it, is YES; so is work the contract sum already obliges the contractor to perform (its own rework or punch-list items, an activity within a milestone) billed as a separate line. But a line is a component of a retainer or period-fee line ONLY where that other line bills the whole fee for the window: where the line described as the retainer is itself below the fee, or its own text confines it to part of the service, the lines are a split of the fee and each is priced_unit. Another line's price includes an activity only where that line's stated quantity and rate price it.

Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is work BEYOND the priced units (an hourly or daily add-on on a fixed-fee, retainer or milestone contract; a change; extra units) AND the packet shows it was approved in writing before or when it was done: a change order, a PO line for it, an email or approval comment from the designated approver naming it, or a verbal emergency approval that the contract itself permits. NO if the line is the priced work itself, or if no such written approval is in the packet. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. A change order is shown only where the change order itself, or a record of ours recording its approval, is in the packet; a record that merely mentions a change-order number does not show it. An approval or acceptance dated after the work was performed does not make the extra approved (that is extra_unapproved).

Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is work of a covered KIND beyond the priced units (an hourly or daily add-on on a fixed-fee, retainer or milestone contract; extra units; a change) WITHOUT written approval in the packet: a verbal request the contract does not provide for, a later tracker mention, an owner who says they asked informally, a pre-approval the packet never shows. NO if the line is the priced work itself, if written approval is in the packet, or if the work is of a kind the authorization never describes at all. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Also YES for in-scope work billed on a basis the contract does not provide (hourly or daily on a lump-sum, fixed-fee or milestone contract); for a line ordered without any purchase order under a framework agreement that authorizes work only through purchase orders; and for work the scope text admits only by change order when no change order is shown.

Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is NOT the work the authorization describes at all: a different service, deliverable or project, a kind of work the contract or PO scope text never mentions, or an item the PO or owner explicitly excludes. NO for an add-on of a covered kind that merely lacks its own approval, and for a line whose wording is too vague to place. If the invoice's bill-to entity or vendor does not match its purchase order, the review stops before scope matters: answer YES to priced_unit and NO to every other scope option. Work the contract's scope text expressly excludes is not_ours even if a change order could have added it. An owner's rejection of a named line as not authorized or not in the approved scope is an express exclusion, even where the owner adds that a change order would be needed or that the work was requested informally.
UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

question: If invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") bills work or goods: what do OUR OWN records establish about whether it was performed or delivered for the billed period? Pick one. The vendor's own documents never move a line out of vendor_only.
options: OUR OWN records (a goods receipt, receiving confirmation, acceptance record, owner tracker note, owner comment or an unqualified owner approval) say the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") were delivered or performed as billed for the billed period or milestone, or delivered with only the formal sign-off still pending. A record that describes the deliverable as a whole confirms every line of it. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality. NO if our record says less or nothing was done, if only the vendor's own documents describe it, or if nothing describes it. A record describing the deliverable or service period as a whole confirms every line the packet places within it, including hourly or add-on lines for that period, unless it names the line's work as missing or incomplete; a record that itemises what it reviewed confirms only the items it names, and a record that names the period or deliverable and then lists what it comprised or what was checked IS an itemising record. Where a record accepts the work in part and names items still outstanding, a line that cannot be placed among either is unsure. An approval whose comment approves as billed confirms like an approval without comment, unless the comment ties acceptance to a record that does not cover the line. A delivered item with a minor, remediable defect is confirmed. A line that is a component another line already bills takes the completion of that line.

OUR OWN record says LESS was done or delivered on invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") than the line bills: a lower percent complete, fewer units or a smaller headcount, components not fitted, deliverables the owner says are missing, receiving short (an acceptance record, or a goods receipt when there is no acceptance record). Only the buyer's own words count. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality; a goods receipt plainly wrong for lines other records verify is disregarded. NO if our record says nothing was done at all, if the disagreement is about whether the work was AUTHORISED (scope) or about price, or if the only conflicting document is the vendor's. Also YES for a deliverable our record says was delivered but nonconforming or requiring revision before acceptance. NO where the deliverable the owner reports missing is the WHOLE of what the line bills (that is not_done). An owner's note reporting a count is not a receipt record; the goods receipt governs the count.

Our own records, or the vendor's own admission in the thread, say the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") have NOT HAPPENED AT ALL: not started, nothing delivered, milestone not reached. Partly done, done differently, fewer units or a lower percent complete is NO (that is 'less'). A milestone billed before its acceptance with no record saying the work has not happened is NO. A single deliverable that the owner's record says has not been received is not_done, not less.

The ONLY evidence describing the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is the vendor's own: its service log, its report, its delivery note, its timesheet. Nothing from our side (receipt, receiving, acceptance, owner note or an approval without comment) describes this line's work as delivered, short or not done. NO only if such a record of ours exists (a note that our review is still pending is not one), or if nothing at all describes it. The vendor's own evidence includes a timesheet or transmittal reproduced on or attached to the invoice, and the vendor's assertion in an email or in the invoice's own narrative that the work was performed. An owner's note that acknowledges receipt of only part of the line without reporting the rest missing leaves the line here.

NOTHING in the packet describes the work or goods on invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") as delivered or performed for the billed period: no record of ours and no vendor document either. Unqualified owner approval of the invoice counts as our record (then NO). A record describing a deliverable as a whole confirms only lines the packet places within that deliverable; a line the packet does not so place, described nowhere but by its own text and amount, is none.
UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

question: If invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") bills work or goods: what do OUR OWN records establish about whether it was performed or delivered for the billed period? Pick one. The vendor's own documents never move a line out of vendor_only.
options: OUR OWN records (a goods receipt, receiving confirmation, acceptance record, owner tracker note, owner comment or an unqualified owner approval) say the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") were delivered or performed as billed for the billed period or milestone, or delivered with only the formal sign-off still pending. A record that describes the deliverable as a whole confirms every line of it. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality. NO if our record says less or nothing was done, if only the vendor's own documents describe it, or if nothing describes it. A record describing the deliverable or service period as a whole confirms every line the packet places within it, including hourly or add-on lines for that period, unless it names the line's work as missing or incomplete; a record that itemises what it reviewed confirms only the items it names, and a record that names the period or deliverable and then lists what it comprised or what was checked IS an itemising record. Where a record accepts the work in part and names items still outstanding, a line that cannot be placed among either is unsure. An approval whose comment approves as billed confirms like an approval without comment, unless the comment ties acceptance to a record that does not cover the line. A delivered item with a minor, remediable defect is confirmed. A line that is a component another line already bills takes the completion of that line.

OUR OWN record says LESS was done or delivered on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") than the line bills: a lower percent complete, fewer units or a smaller headcount, components not fitted, deliverables the owner says are missing, receiving short (an acceptance record, or a goods receipt when there is no acceptance record). Only the buyer's own words count. When our records disagree, the acceptance record, then the goods receipt, governs the count and an owner note governs degree and quality; a goods receipt plainly wrong for lines other records verify is disregarded. NO if our record says nothing was done at all, if the disagreement is about whether the work was AUTHORISED (scope) or about price, or if the only conflicting document is the vendor's. Also YES for a deliverable our record says was delivered but nonconforming or requiring revision before acceptance. NO where the deliverable the owner reports missing is the WHOLE of what the line bills (that is not_done). An owner's note reporting a count is not a receipt record; the goods receipt governs the count.

Our own records, or the vendor's own admission in the thread, say the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") have NOT HAPPENED AT ALL: not started, nothing delivered, milestone not reached. Partly done, done differently, fewer units or a lower percent complete is NO (that is 'less'). A milestone billed before its acceptance with no record saying the work has not happened is NO. A single deliverable that the owner's record says has not been received is not_done, not less.

The ONLY evidence describing the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") is the vendor's own: its service log, its report, its delivery note, its timesheet. Nothing from our side (receipt, receiving, acceptance, owner note or an approval without comment) describes this line's work as delivered, short or not done. NO only if such a record of ours exists (a note that our review is still pending is not one), or if nothing at all describes it. The vendor's own evidence includes a timesheet or transmittal reproduced on or attached to the invoice, and the vendor's assertion in an email or in the invoice's own narrative that the work was performed. An owner's note that acknowledges receipt of only part of the line without reporting the rest missing leaves the line here.

NOTHING in the packet describes the work or goods on invoice line 3 ("VULN-DASH™ Portal Access — 4 named seats (H. Te Whaiti, J. Prasad, M. Liu, S. Burrows), July 2026") as delivered or performed for the billed period: no record of ours and no vendor document either. Unqualified owner approval of the invoice counts as our record (then NO). A record describing a deliverable as a whole confirms only lines the packet places within that deliverable; a line the packet does not so place, described nowhere but by its own text and amount, is none.
UNSURE: none of the other options is more likely than not; the packet genuinely supports two of them. Not a way to defer a decision you could make.

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

question: What IS invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)")? Pick the one kind that fits, from its own wording and the invoice.
options: Invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)") bills WORK OR GOODS: a service, deliverable, milestone, period of service, labour hours, usage, licences or physical items. Not tax, not a freight/handling/surcharge line, not a credit, discount, rebate, retainage or expense line.

Invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)") IS a tax amount (VAT, GST, IGST, sales tax, HST) charged on the other lines, whatever it is called. Work ABOUT tax (tax advisory, VAT return preparation, a tax compliance calendar) is work, not tax.

Invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)") is a CHARGE ON TOP of the work rather than work itself: freight, shipping, handling, courier, postage, a surcharge, an expediting, admin, processing or minimum charge, or a commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines. Freight booking or dispatch paperwork accompanying goods is a charge on top; a line that itself delivers a service or goods is work.

Invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)") is a CREDIT, discount, rebate or credit-memo line, whether shown negative or (wrongly) positive. It reduces or adjusts what is owed rather than billing work.

Invoice line 2 ("Manual Test-Units — Remediation-Validation Re-Tests (critical findings from June API assessment, SEC-2026-0133)") is an EXPENSE pass-through (travel, per diem, mileage reimbursement) or a retainage / retention release line. Billed usage of a service (fleet mileage as the service itself) is work, not an expense.

Wording, amount or invoice number may differ. Answer NO for a recurring service billing a NEW period (a later month, a later application number) however alike the prior invoices look, for a genuinely later phase or shipment, for a re-bill of a prior invoice that was reversed or credited, and when no prior invoice covers this work. Answer NO where the prior invoice bills this invoice's obligation AS A WHOLE (the same milestone, application, shipment or period that the whole invoice bills, or a re-issue of the same invoice): that is the prior-relation question, not a re-billed line; re-billed is for one old line slipped into an otherwise new invoice. YES for a catch-up or cumulative-adjustment charge for earlier months whose retainer a paid prior invoice already billed. If you cannot point to the specific prior invoice that already billed it, answer NO.

contract.title: Subscription Agreement AGR-2026-09 — Continuous Penetration Testing & Vulnerability Assessment Services
relevant_excerpts: 2. Scope of Services. 2.1 SecureEdge shall provide the Customer with continuous penetration testing and vulnerability assessment services ('Services') targeting the Customer's external and internal network infrastructure, web applications (including the GrantsHub™ portal and DonorConnect interface), and API integration endpoints, as further described in Schedule A. 2.2 Services include automated vulnerability scanning, manual penetration testing, reporting of findings classified per CVSS v3.1, and remediation-validation re-testing upon Customer request. 2.3 The Customer shall consume Services on a metered basis; usage shall be measured in scan-hours (automated scanning engine time) and test-units (each discrete manual test engagement of up to four hours' duration). 2.4 Services expressly exclude red-team physical intrusion testing, social-engineering campaigns, and any testing of third-party hosted SaaS platforms not contractually controlled by the Customer, unless agreed via a Change Order under clause 9.

4. Fees and Invoicing. 4.1 The Customer shall pay for Services consumed during each calendar month in arrears, at the rates set out in Schedule B (Rate Card). 4.2 SecureEdge shall issue a tax invoice by the twentieth (20th) day of the month following the metering period, itemising scan-hours and test-units consumed, with supporting usage logs exported from the VULN-DASH™ portal. 4.3 Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. 4.4 Total fees payable under this Agreement shall not exceed the Purchase Order ceiling of AUD 87,100.00 (inclusive of GST) without prior written approval from the Customer's authorised procurement delegate. 4.5 Where metered consumption in any month would cause aggregate billings to exceed ninety percent (90%) of the PO ceiling, SecureEdge shall notify the Customer's nominated contract manager within two (2) business days.

5. Acceptance. 5.1 Each penetration test report and vulnerability scan summary ('Deliverable') shall be deemed accepted unless the Customer provides written notice of material deficiency within ten (10) business days of delivery via the VULN-DASH™ portal or email to the designated SecureEdge engagement lead. 5.2 Material deficiency is limited to: (a) failure to test the agreed-scope targets; (b) misclassification of findings by two or more CVSS severity bands; or (c) inclusion of data from environments outside the authorised test scope. 5.3 Upon receipt of a deficiency notice, SecureEdge shall remediate and re-deliver within five (5) business days at no additional charge.

9. Changes. 9.1 Either party may propose changes to the scope, rate card, or consumption limits by issuing a written Change Order request referencing this Agreement (AGR-2026-09). 9.2 No Change Order shall be effective unless signed by both parties' authorised representatives. 9.3 Work performed outside the scope defined in clause 2 without an executed Change Order shall not be billable and shall be performed at SecureEdge's own risk. 9.4 If the Customer requests services that SecureEdge reasonably determines fall outside scope, SecureEdge shall promptly notify the Customer in writing (referencing the relevant support ticket) before commencing any such work.

question: Invoice line 1 ("Automated Scan-Hours — Internal Network Vulnerability Scanning (Corporate Services VLANs CS-01–CS-04), July 2026 cycle, ref SEC-2026-0148") is an ADD-ON charge rather than the work or goods themselves: a fee, surcharge, handling, admin, expediting, minimum-charge or adjustment line (a 'coordination fee', not coordination labour on site) that sits on top of the priced work and traces to no PO line, no contract clause, and not to how this vendor has billed before (see prior invoices). A line billing services or goods is NOT a fee however vague its wording ("Consulting services", "Professional fees", "Work performed"); vagueness is a separate question. A credit, discount or rebate line, even shown as a positive amount, is never a fee (it is an adjustment); a tax or expense line is not a fee. Fees the contract or PO text provides for, and charges a PO line prices, are explained; scope prose is not a PO line. A commission or mark-up computed as a percentage of other lines is a charge on top, explained where the contract provides for it.
